$comment: Disclosed exceptions to the full dependency audit. Each entry names ONE
advisory URL and ONE package, must carry a written justification, and
expires on a stated date. Expired entries stop applying and fail the audit,
so an exception cannot become permanent by neglect. The production audit
never consults this file: anything reaching a shipped artifact blocks
unconditionally. Add an entry only when there is no available remediation,

exceptions.justification: Stack exhaustion denial of service (CVE-2026-93687, high) when braces expands a deeply nested brace pattern. No remediation is available: the advisory covers every release up to 3.0.3 and names no patched version, 3.0.3 is the latest braces release on the npm registry, the latest micromatch (4.0.8) depends on braces ^3.0.3 and the latest fast-glob (3.3.3) reaches it through micromatch ^4.0.8, and the upstream issue is open with no released fix (an unmerged community fix, micromatch/braces pull request 72, is the signal to watch), so neither a lockfile update nor an override has a version to move to. Verified 2026-10-03. braces is reached only through eslint-config-next, @next/eslint-plugin-next, fast-glob and micromatch, which expand glob patterns taken from committed lint configuration and never from untrusted input. It is absent from the production audit set and from the production dependency tree, so it does not reach a shipped build. Remove this entry when braces or micromatch publishes a fixed release (for example once pull request 72 is released), or when eslint-config-next no longer reaches fast-glob, whichever comes first, and in any case renew or remove it by the expiry date.
